---
title: "Adaptive step-up regularization"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Adaptive step-up regularization}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
```

REPAIR's modified method of moments subtracts sampling-error moments from the
observed moments. Weak predictor information can make the corrected system
poorly conditioned. The manuscript's step-up variant (M-MOMS) selects two
regularization constants sequentially, using numerical conditioning criteria.
The default remains fixed minimum regularization.

```{r fit}
data(repair_example)
model <- lme4::lmer(score ~ day + (day | person), repair_example$repeated)
fit <- repair(practice ~ re("day"), model, repair_example$people, "person",
  regularization = "step_up")
repair_coefficients(fit)
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "regularization")
```

The preliminary search starts at `q + 2`, with q predictor columns excluding
the intercept. It chooses a preliminary alpha, recomputes residual variance and
inverse case-variance weights, and then chooses the final alpha. The two alphas
can differ. `regularization = "none"` still subtracts measurement error; it only
disables regularization.

Each search uses nine equally spaced candidates up to `N` or `N * lambda - 1`,
according to the determinant-root branch. The upper bound stops the search from
turning subtraction into addition when a nonnegative multiplier is attainable
above the minimum. A missing root or upper bound below the minimum leaves only
the minimum-alpha candidate. After finding a passing candidate, at most 12
bisections refine the interval from the preceding failing candidate, stopping at
an alpha gap of 0.005. The selected value is the smallest passing value evaluated.

A candidate must produce a usable complete fit. The corrected predictor block,
excluding the intercept, must have minimum eigenvalue at least
`sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)`, corrected-minimum/observed-maximum eigenvalue ratio
at least .05, and condition number at most 100,000. Preliminary moments are
divided by N; final weighted moments are sums, matching the research algorithm.
These criteria depend on predictor units and are not a coverage guarantee.

```{r search}
search <- summary(fit)$diagnostics$step_up
search$preliminary$selected
search$final$selected
head(search$preliminary$candidates)
```

If no candidate passes, the algorithm returns the minimum-alpha fit and marks
`fallback = TRUE`, `met_criteria = FALSE`. If that fit also fails numerically,
the returned result remains a numerical failure. A converged fallback must not
be described as satisfying the conditioning criteria. `summary(fit)` reports
this distinction.

Search settings can be supplied explicitly. Choose them as part of the analysis
specification; changing a threshold changes the estimator.

```{r controls}
stricter <- repair(practice ~ re("day"), model, repair_example$people, "person",
  regularization = "step_up",
  step_up_control = list(min_relative_eigenvalue = .999))
repair_diagnostics(stricter, table = "regularization")
lapply(summary(stricter)$diagnostics$step_up,
  function(x) x[c("alpha", "met_criteria", "fallback", "reason")])
```

See `?fit_mmom` for all settings. Advanced callers can give separate preliminary
and final policies using `list(correction = "step_up", step_up = list(...))` in
the corresponding `fit_mmom()` controls. The conditional covariance calculation
uses the selected moments and weights. It does not account for first-stage
parameter estimation or establish post-selection coverage.

`repair_refit()` and `repair_bootstrap()` preserve the requested search policy
and reselect both alphas on every new dataset. They do not freeze the original
selected constants. Bootstrap diagnostics retain each attempt's selected alphas
and conditioning/fallback indicators, along with the existing failure audit.

```{r bootstrap}
# Three attempts demonstrate the interface, not adequate tail precision.
boot <- repair_bootstrap(fit, repair_example$repeated, repair_example$people,
  B = 3, seed = 41)
repair_bootstrap_diagnostics(boot)[, c("replicate", "usable",
  "preliminary_alpha", "final_alpha", "preliminary_criteria_met",
  "final_criteria_met", "preliminary_fallback", "final_fallback")]
```

The bootstrap is experimental and retains its strict default failure policy.
See `vignette("person-bootstrap")` for its scope, percentile intervals, and
success-conditional inference. No influence-function, leverage, or delete-one
inference methods are included in this release.
